Alex R: Hey folks — putting together a concise runbook for preemptible GPU drains + automated fallback. Want to capture operator steps, Pager thresholds, and a small automation snippet we can land in infra-runbooks.
Maria P: 👍 Important we include exact kubectl/eviction commands and a short PromQL alert to detect mass evictions.
Chen L: Also list the expected behavior when mixed pools are active: how routing moves from preemptible to on-demand, and how autoscaler should behave.
Priya S: Can we add a short escalation matrix? e.g., 1) 1–2 node evictions -> SRE triage; 2) >10% capacity loss -> page; 3) sustained >5min fallback to on-demand -> exec notify.
Alex R: Draft runbook outline below. Please comment inline.

Alex R: RUNBOOK: Preemptible GPU Drain & Fallback — quick reference
- Goal: graceful eviction handling for preemptible GPUs, ensure minimal application disruption, and trigger fallback routing/scale-up when needed.
- Scope: GPU clusters using mixed-preemptible and on-demand pools for inference fleets.

Steps (operator):
1) Verify alerts: `grafana -> Alerts` or check Prometheus query `sum(rate(node_preemptions_total[5m])) by (zone)`
2) Confirm draining nodes: `kubectl get nodes -l gpu-type=preemptible` then `kubectl cordon <node>` and `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` if safe.
3) Check pods evicted: `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Failed -o wide | grep Evicted` and identify critical pods (inference services).
4) Trigger fallback policy if >X pods evicted or node count reduced >Y% (automation will handle; manual fallback command below).

Automation snippet (bash):
```
# coarse example: if preemptible pool drops below threshold, trigger on-demand scale-up
PREEM_NODES=$(gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"labels=gpu=preemptible\" --format=\"value(name)\" | wc -l)
if [ \"$PREEM_NODES\" -lt 3 ]; then
  # use infra API to increase on-demand pool replicas
  curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN\" https://infra-api.internal/v1/pools/on-demand/scale -d '{\"replicas\":10}'
  slack-cli --channel #eng-infra --message \"[runbook] preemptible pool low ($PREEM_NODES). Requested on-demand scale-up to 10\"
fi
```

Escalation matrix (concise):
- Warning (no page): transient 1–2 preemptions in <5m. Owner: infra team.
- Page SRE: >=5 preemptions across >1 zone in 10m OR capacity loss >15%.
- Page Engineering leader + infra on-call: sustained fallback for >15m or degraded latency >2x P95.

On-call messages (templates):
- Short alert (auto): `oncall-bot: preemptible-pool-evictions detected in us-west1: 6 in 10m. Auto-fallback triggered.`
- Manual escalation: `@oncall @sre Please triage — mass preemptions affecting inference fleet. Runbook: <link>`

Post-incident checklist:
- Record which workloads were affected and fallback timing.
- Adjust autoscaler thresholds if noisy preemptions are common.
- Consider moving stable critical services to on-demand/dedicated capacity.
- Create an RCA if >30min disruption.

Operational notes:
- Prefer graceful drain to avoid cold-starts for models with large KV caches.
- Use node-labels to preserve placement: `kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.labels}'` on critical pods.
- Cost tradeoffs: fallback to on-demand will increase unit cost; include estimated cost delta in incident summary.

Maria P: Add PromQL samples for the alerts? I'd propose:
`sum(rate(kube_node_status_condition{condition=\"Preempting\"}[5m])) by (zone)`
`sum(kube_node_status_capacity_gpu{job=\"kube-state-metrics\"})` to track capacity.

Chen L: Add a quick runbook-safe checklist for teams deploying models: tag workloads with `preemptible-tolerant=true/false` so autoscaler and routing know which to move.

Priya S: Agree. Also add a short note about network egress and AZ constraints — some regions have limited ephemeral GPU quotas; rolling fallback may need cross-AZ traffic considerations.

Alex R: Great feedback. I'll incorporate these and push to infra-runbooks repo. Final ask: reviewers — please sign off or submit edits in the PR by EOD.
